bodyText:

[Forwarded from Stephen E. Chappelear, Jan 28 2024:] Mark, this report will give you a status update on our case... We spent some time in the discovery phase of the case. The State sent a Request for Admissions, and a Request for Production of Documents to us; we submitted the same to Mullins Bros. There were 4 depositions taken: Steve Mullins, his attorney Bob Rauzi, Cloyd Yough, and Steve Mullins again.
We filed summary judgment motions as to the State, and Mullins, arguing the only basis for finding someone responsible for repairs to the Dam is if they "own" the Dam, and the homeowners in Phase VII and VIII do not own the Dam; also that the Declarations do not change that result (inadequate notice, no individual maintenance liability, Declarations only refer to maintenance of the lake not the Dam).
Mullins filed its motion for summary judgment as to our cross-claim against Mullins. The State and Mullins filed responses; we filed a response to Mullins' motion; replies to responses were filed by both sides. Briefing is now complete on the various summary judgment motions.
Mullins also filed a motion seeking permission to file an amended cross-claim against the homeowners in Phase VII and VIII, alleging each signed an agreement acknowledging the Declaration and agreeing to join an HOA and pay $200/year; we opposed that motion.
Several individuals sold their homes and wish to be dismissed; State agreed to substitute new owners as parties, Mullins did not, so we filed a motion for substitution (unopposed by Mullins, ripe for decision). Steve

bodyText: Dear Neighbors, I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to inform you of my decision to resign from my position as a member of the HOA Board, effective September 6, 2024. However, due to personal and professional commitments, I find that I am unable to dedicate the necessary time and energy to fulfill my responsibilities on the Board effectively. subject: RE: HOA Board suggestions requested
bodyText:
Cindy: I am sorry to hear that you are leaving the HOA board, but I understand the impulse to do so.
To all: I was hoping my email (sent out over a year ago!) would stimulate a different reaction from you and the rest of the HOA board members. But I have heard nothing until now.
First, for the benefit of those remaining, our insurance was paid in July 2024 and we are all covered until July 2025.
Second, I understand that everyone is probably trying to lay low until the lake/dam issue is resolved.
But the main problem remains: Without further action, our HOA will die with a whimper in less than a year. Without action, we must have a vote of the full membership to make the decision on dissolving/continuing the HOA.

subject: Re: HOA Board suggestions requested
bodyText: Dear Mike and Fellow Board Members, As most of you know, I proposed to abolish this HOA before. In my opinion, we inherited more bad side effects than benefits from an organization that was not our own creation, whose rules we did not write. I was thinking we should wait until the litigation is concluded. But it is taking too long. It is plainly clear that there is not enough interest from the residents to keep the HOA functional. In my opinion, it is time to abolish it. I think the main item of business in February 2025 should be to vote on abolishing it. Best, Noah

subject: RE: HOA Board suggestions requested
bodyText: To all: Thanks to Nuh for your response. And I agree with your conclusion that we must have a meeting of the full HOA to decide the matter of whether to keep the HOA or not. I disagree that it will "automatically dissolve" if there is no participation. There are some questions that need to be answered: 1. How best to ensure all residents get to vote (quorum required to dissolve, possibly vote by email and in person, update resident contact list). 2. If the vote is YES to keep the HOA, we must elect new board members right away. 3. The first big issue will be to re-instate annual dues (requires setting up payment procedure and enforcement).

subject: KCCD Ruling
bodyText:
Good Morning All,
I have attached the Judge's decision on the summary judgment motions, which was filed yesterday.
The decision is a bit of a mixed bag. It does not resolve the entire case.
Here is a summary of the critical findings made by the Judge.
1. The individual landowners are not the owners of the Dam.
2. The owner of the Dam is The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.
3. Because The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc. had its articles of incorporation cancelled in 2015, the court is going to appoint a receiver to act on behalf of the corporation. The receiver will be charged with the responsibility to move forward with making a decision on what should be done with the Dam, subject to approval by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources.
4. The residents of Phases VII and VIII are bound by the Declarations which were filed with the County Recorder.
5. The Declarations require all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance."
6. The "lake" includes the Dam.
The Judge has not decided at this time who will have to pay the cost of remediation of the Dam, or ongoing expenses. This will be determined at trial. It is possible that the Judge could find that the homeowners in Phases VII and VIII were required by the Declarations to be members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.; which was a mistaken name and should have been The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc., and is therefore changed to that; that the Declarations require the homeowners to pay assessments issued by the corporation for common expenses; that the receiver will issue assessments against each homeowner for the cost of repairing and maintaining the Dam. There are also other possibilities.
On October 3, the Judge will appoint a receiver. We will attempt to influence the appointment of the receiver, so we have some say over the remedy or some way to control/influence the cost.
I recommend we contact a structural engineer to review this as the dam repair may be as simple as lowing the spillway. We have never had the opportunity to ask.

subject: RE: KCCD Ruling
bodyText: Mark, if this plays out the way it appears I think we need to have Steve see if he can find a good engineer to evaluate the dam and make recommendations to us as apposed to having the City do it. They will want to make things out to work in their favor since everyone else will be paying for it.

subject: Re: KCCD Ruling
bodyText: Hi Lee, I am walking the Dam with dam excavator this week to get a quotation started. Should be interesting.

subject: Re: KCCD Ruling
bodyText: How do we speak directly to the judge to inform him that when to lake/dam was transferred to Mullins and the to most of the home owners, that the dam was classified a class 2. subject: Re: KCCD Ruling
bodyText:
Mark, Thanks for the copy and the summary. I have read the court document. I have a concern with a fact that the judge seems to have glossed over. The "Developer" no longer owns the land. The court documents make it very clear that The Landings Property Owners, Inc. owns the land. The Declarations state very clearly that, all lot owners to become members of the Landings Common Area Association, Inc., which "shall have the sole and exclusive control of the lake located on the land of the Developer and shall be responsible for its care and maintenance." Although the judge made an effort to emphasize certain components clause, he failed to recognize that, in that same clause, the terms apply to lake on the land of the developer. My question: If the Developer no longer owns the land is the clause still valid?
Thanks, Jesse

subject: RE: KCCD Ruling
bodyText: Jesse, the short answer to your question is that yes, the clause is still valid. The court is well aware of the points you made in your message. Steve

subject: RE: KCCD Ruling
bodyText:
To fellow homeowners:
These questions and suggestions reflect the thoughts of many of us. I would just like to point out that, based on the summary that Mark gave us of Judge Wetzel's ruling (and assuming it holds up), the HOA (not the individual homeowners) will be the responsible party for resolving the dam/lake issue (items #1,2, and 4).
Unfortunately, our HOA is currently non-functional and essentially out of money. Debbie Banda and I tried desperately to warn of this impending situation at our HOA meeting in February 2023. No one stepped forward to be officers of the Board. In the meantime, I have sent out emails multiple times trying to get people interested in having a meeting and coming up with suggestions concerning the fate of the HOA. I have gotten zero help on this issue except from Debbie Banda.
So now there are two crunches coming: the final trial decision and the death of our HOA by neglect, exactly at the time when we need to be well-organized to make important decisions as a unified organization.
Now maybe I am wrong about some (or all) of this, but I would really, really like to have an open conversation about it. It is only fair that the WHOLE HOA be involved in any decisions concerning: Existence of the HOA; Election of a working board with actual officers who lead the way; Re-instituting annual dues; How to face the consequences of the final decision on the dam/lake.
Note: Debbie and I are trying once again to get the HOA board moving. Debbie has kindly volunteered to have a meeting at her house sometime in October (current board only, not the full HOA). If it helps get people to come, there will be wine and hors d'oeuvres.
If this initial board meeting is fruitful, we will get the full HOA involved at a later time, TBD.
I think we need get organized NOW.
P.S. If anyone out there would like to volunteer for HOA board leadership, please let me know. We need a president, vice president, and treasurer (since I (current treasurer) am going to retire). Also note the treasurer job is easy; WRP CPAs handle tax returns/audits.
Mike

bodyText:
Dear All, I do not know if anyone attended the hearing yesterday to appoint a receiver. I participated by phone.
1. Jeff Harris was appointed as the receiver. I learned from Steve Chappelear's comment that Jeff is not among the Long Defendants. Chappelear suggested that the receiver should be among the residents of Long Defendants. I totally agree with that. I did not know that Jeff's new house is not in Phase 7 or 8. Given the complicated roles Jeff held so far, and his move of residence, I am particularly suspicious of his being a receiver.
2. At the end of the hearing, a couple of the residents shared some concerns. One of them mentioned responsibilities of the city that led to this situation (granting building permits for so many houses and development). Judge Wetzel dismissed those concerns saying something like "it does not matter how we got here." Another neighbor (Mrs. Risser) commented about the unfairness of the decision. The judge acknowledged the unfairness but went ahead with the decision anyway.

subject: Re: KCCD Status
bodyText: I MUST BE MISSING SOMETHING. Why is the City directing all of this? Looks like to me that we should doing things to satisfy ODNR. It is ODNR we should be satisfying not the City.The City is the one that has made this a mess in the beginning and now we are letting them be the lead. They are setting us up. Cloyd Yough

subject: Re: KCCD Status
bodyText: City is leading for two reasons. 1. They have control of the ARPA funding and 2. the judge has assigned them to lead the repair. This is important from an engineering and construction standpoint as it effectively transfers any engineering liability the city and ODNR. ODNR remains the approving authority but the ODNR would direct their approval to the engineer/contractor in approving the solution. We are in a delicate position. We need to keep enough distance to allow engineering liability toward the City and State while providing just enough input on the solution to get the result we want but not so much that we don't signal any agreement that accept the position of payor for the repair.
